 Judgment

"Whether the Tribunal committed illegality in fastening the liability to the appellant/insurer to pay
the compensation?"
is the question involved in this case.
2. The appellant was respondent No.2, re
spondent Nos.1 and 2 were claimants Nos.1 and 2,
Respondent No.3 was the first respondent in MVC No.226/2009 on the file of the MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, SCCH-4.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the purpose of convenience, the parties will be referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the husband and minor daughter of deceased Geetha Prakash.
Geetha Prakash was employed in the first respondent's organization as Accounts Executive.

On 21.08.2008 at 11.10 p.m. when Geetha Prakash and her two other colleagues were travelling in Maruthi 800 Car bearing registration No.KA.05-MA-2694 owned by respondent No.2 to Punganur in Andhra Pradesh to attend a marriage of their colleague, near Vadagur tank within the limits of Kolar Rural police station, the driver of the car hit the road guard stone and toppled into the tank.
In the accident Geetha Prakash suffered grievous injuries.

She was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar,
and she succumbed to injuries.
4.
Regarding the accident one Somoji Rao filed complaint before the Kolar Rural police.
Based on the complaint, Kolar Rural police registered FIR as per Ex.P1 against the driver of the car.
On investigation, charge sheet as per Ex.P5 was filed against the driver of the Car.

At the relevant time the offending Car was insured with respondent No.2.
5.

Claimants filed MVC No.226/2009 before the MACT, Court of Small Causes (SCCH-4),
Bangalore, against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.45,70,000/- on the ground that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car.

Bangalore

sentences.text: They further claimed that they were the dependents of the deceased and due to her death they have suffered the damages.

6. Respondent No.2 alone contested the petition denying the rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of car, age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2 also contended that the deceased being the employee of respondent No.1 becomes Legal Manager vs K R Prakash on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184052682/
2 his representative.

sentences.text:
Thus she cannot compensate for the tortious act or vicarious liability of respondent No.1.
7.

The Tribunal on recording the evidence of the parties and on hearing them by the impugned award allowed the petition granting compensation of Rs.16,93,536/- with interest thereon at 6% per annum payable by the appellant.
The appellant filed review petition pending this appeal.
The Tribunal by order dated 10.04.2015 reviewed its award dated 04.03.2014 on the ground that there were arithmetical errors in calculating the compensation.

By the said award, the Tribunal modified the compensation from Rs.16,93,536/- to 25,44,360/-
8.

The sole ground of challenge in this case is that the policy did not cover the risk of the occupant of the car, Geetha Prakash does not become the third party, therefore the Tribunal should not have fastened the liability to the insurer.
Ex.R.1 shows that the appellant had received the premium to cover the personal accident benefit.
Therefore there is no merit in the contention that the risk of the personal accident was not covered.
Since the deceased was not traveling during the course of her duty or in discharge of her duty, she cannot be treated as a workmen within the meaning of Workmen's Compensation Act.
9. RW.1 in his cross-examination unequivocally admitted that Ex.R1 the policy covers personal accident and the third party liability both.
He also admitted that the policy is comprehensive policy and on such policy the third party risk and own damage are covered.
He admitted that, it includes coverage for the death and bodily injury of any person or occupant of the car.

10. In the similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment of National Insurance Company Limited Vs Balakrishnan and Another1 discussing in detail in para Nos.21 to 24 and 26 of the judgment about the direction issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDA) and Tariff Advisory Committee (TAC) has held that in the case (2012)1 SCC 731 of comprehensive policy/package policy, the insurer are bound to pay the compensation in respect of the liability towards an occupant in a car.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs Balakrishnan and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further held that such policy would cover the liability of the insurer for payment of compensation for the occupant in a car.
In view of said judgment, there is no merit in the contention of the insurer that the policy did not cover the risk of the occupant of car.
Therefore the appeal deserves no merit.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The amount in deposit and the TCRs shall be transmitted to the trial Court forthwith.
